title: The Fox and the Grapes
text:
A hungry fox was trotting along a country road when he saw a vine climbing over a high trellis. From it hung bunches of grapes, dark, ripe and heavy with juice. His mouth watered at the sight.

He backed up, ran and leaped for the nearest bunch, but his jaws snapped shut on empty air a little below it. He tried again, jumping higher, and again he missed. He tried from a different angle, and then from a running start, and then again and again, until he was panting and his legs ached. The grapes still hung just out of reach.

At last he gave up. He sat down, caught his breath, and looked up at the vine with a sniff. Those grapes, he said to himself, were plainly sour. Nobody with any sense would want them. He was glad he had not wasted any more effort on such poor fruit.

Then he put his nose in the air and walked off down the road, telling himself that he had never really wanted them at all.
lesson: When you fail to get something, notice if you suddenly decide it was worthless. Rationalizing a loss feels better, but it stops you from learning why you failed or whether to try another way.
